title: Console Coreway: Semantic Sidebar + Workspace Flow Prototype
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Redesign the Redwood Console primary navigation to reduce cognitive overhead for multi-workspace users and introduce a semantic, collapsible sidebar that surfaces: prioritized dashboards, active rollouts, and a cost lens. Produce clickable prototypes for usability testing and hand off tokenized components to engineering.
acceptance_criteria: New sidebar prototype implements three semantic rails: Explore, Monitor, Control
Workspace switcher accessible in two clicks for >90% of common flows
Dashboard tiles offer an at-a-glance cost delta with hover drilldown
Rollouts panel supports canary toggle and quick rollback affordances
Design tokens and spacing spec delivered for dev handoff (Figma + tokens.json)
Usability test score: median task completion >= 85% on workspace switch and find-rollback flows
design_notes: Goal: reduce top-level items from 12 to 7 by grouping related console surfaces into semantic rails
Semantic rails: Explore (catalog, models), Monitor (dashboards, alerts, logs), Control (rollouts, capacity, billing)
Introduce a compact state (icons only) and expanded state (icons + microlabels) to support narrow viewports and parked workflows
Role-aware ordering: engineers see Monitor first; admins see Control first. Ordering controlled by lightweight policy in user prefs
Workspace switcher evolves into an inline overlay with recent/ pinned workspaces and keyboard nav (cmd-k style)
decisions: Opted for rail-based grouping over foldered nav to reduce depth and speed discoverability
Use microlabels (6–10px) for expanded state and hide them in compact to preserve single-column density
Cost lens will surface 24h and 7d deltas; not the full billing page, to minimize cognitive context switching
Rollouts quick-control will favor 'pause' and 'rollback' actions; destructive actions require confirmation modal
tradeoffs: Grouping reduces discoverability of rare surfaces — mitigated by persistent command-palette shortcuts and search
Semantic ordering requires server-side preference mapping for user roles; adds complexity to auth layer
Compact icon-only rail improves vertical real estate but may increase time-to-target for new users — onboarding tour proposed
review_feedback: PM Marcus Chen: prefer Control rail to be first for enterprise orgs; request AB test to validate order
Eng lead Priya Reddy: flagged server-side preference mapping; recommended fallback ordering when prefs missing
Security Samir Kapoor: ask to ensure RBAC hides admin-only controls in Control rail when user lacks permission
UX Research Elena Morales: suggested microcopy changes for rollback confirmation to reduce fear of action
usability_findings: Participants confused by 'Rollouts' nested under Monitor — moved to Control in iteration 2
Cost delta chips were highly visible; hover drilldown used in 83% of trials when present
next_steps: Incorporate review feedback and update prototype (due 2025-02-21)
Prepare design tokens package and open GH PR for style tokens (owner: Lena)
Coordinate with Eng on lightweight API for role-aware ordering (owner: Priya)
Run second usability round focused on admins (target end 2025-02-26)
notes_for_engineering: Provide a /user/preferences endpoint to store rail ordering and compact/expanded state
Expose a minimal feature flag for progressive rollout of compact rail behavior
Dashboard tiles should accept lightweight payload with cost_delta_24h and cost_delta_7d to avoid heavy queries
